extracted.intended_audience: AI researchers and practitioners, technology-transfer professionals, and patent portfolio managers interested in automated patent valuation/pruning
extracted.subtask_description: Designing and evaluating an AI-driven, multi-stage system to prune patent portfolios by identifying high-value assets for technology transfer using a Learning-to-Rank model combined with market-need analysis and agent-based matching.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation against legal and commercial parameters
rubrics_metrics.description: LTR model evaluates patents against over 30 legal and commercial parameters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a broad set of legal and commercial features (30+) as inputs to the evaluation model; these parameters form the basis for scoring/ranking patent assets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learning-to-Rank (LTR) prioritization
rubrics_metrics.description: A Learning to Rank (LTR) model ranks patents to identify high value assets for technology transfer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Train an LTR model to produce an ordered prioritization of patents based on the evaluated parameters, enabling systematic selection/pruning decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need Agent — market need mining
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'Need Agent' uses Natural Language Processing (NLP) to mine unstructured market and industry data, identifying explicit technological needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Automate extraction of explicit market/industry needs from unstructured sources (reports, web data, etc.) to produce demand-side signals that inform patent valuation and matching.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seed Agent — patent claim analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'Seed Agent' employs fine tuned Large Language Models (LLMs) to analyze patent claims and map their technological capabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use fine-tuned LLMs to parse and semantically characterize patent claims, producing capability representations ('Seeds') for downstream matching to market needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core Ontology Framework for Seed-Need matching
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'Core Ontology Framework' matches high potential patents (Seeds) to documented market demands (Needs), providing a strategic rationale for divestment decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Build or leverage an ontology to align patent capability representations with extracted market needs; the matching step yields explainable rationale for selecting patents to keep, divest, or license.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dynamic parameter weighting system
rubrics_metrics.description: A dynamic parameter weighting system adjusts the relative importance of evaluation parameters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement adjustable/dynamic weighting of the legal and commercial parameters so the ranking adapts to context, priorities, or changing market signals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) validation protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: A crucial Human in the-Loop (HITL) validation protocol to ensure both adaptability and real-world credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include human oversight/validation steps to review model outputs, calibrate weights, and confirm mappings, ensuring decisions are credible and actionable for technology transfer stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference for automated, forward-looking analysis over retrospective/manual approaches
rubrics_metrics.description: The framework automates and deepens the patent valuation process as an alternative to methods that rely on retrospective indicators or manual, time intensive analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize automated, demand-driven, and forward-looking signals (e.g., current market needs) rather than solely historical/retrospective indicators; reduce manual effort by integrating NLP/LLM-driven components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide strategic rationale for divestment/selection decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: System outputs should provide a strategic rationale for divestment decisions by matching patent capabilities to market demands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the framework's results are explainable and actionable, supporting strategic decisions about which patents to divest, retain, or pursue for licensing/transfer.
